correctness.summary: A successful partial 3-colouring of a path must leave an independent set of internal vertices uncoloured. For a fixed omitted set U and a proper full 3-colouring encoded by its initial colour and ±1 edge differences in Z_3, each omitted vertex imposes one equality on a disjoint adjacent pair of edge differences. Hence an omitted independent j-set admits exactly 3·2^(n-1-j) compatible full colourings, and there are binomial(n-1-j,j) such sets. This proves the coefficient formula; all stated recurrences and extremal domain counts follow. Definition-level exhaustive checks agree for every P_n with 2≤n≤8 and independently confirm the corrected P_3 value.

originality.scope: to the best of our knowledge
originality.summary: The accessible full texts of arXiv:2609.17108v1 and arXiv:2406.15746 were inspected. The 2026 source gives the two-colour bipartite theorem, the high-colour maximum-degree simplification, and examples through four vertices, but no general path formula; targeted searches under forced/forcing colouring/coloring, paths, partial 3-colourings, chromatic forcing, and graph-polynomial formulations found no equivalent path coefficient law or recurrence. The full 1994 Acta Informatica paper was not inspected and is the strongest identified residual coverage risk; unindexed or differently-termed work remains possible.

value.summary: The result determines the complete forcing-domain distribution for 3-colouring paths and, together with known two-colour and high-colour results, gives the forced-colouring polynomial of every path for every positive number of colours. It yields a Fibonacci-type recurrence, exact minimum forcing-domain size and count, asymptotic enumeration, and corrects a displayed three-vertex special case in the current 2026 preprint.

limitations: The new coefficient theorem is specific to paths and three colours.
The lambda=2 and lambda>=4 branches use results already present in the 2026 source.
The full 1994 Acta Informatica paper was not inspected and is the strongest identified residual prior-coverage risk.
Finite exhaustive computation supports but does not replace the proof.
Unindexed recent work or substantially different terminology may conceal equivalent results.
Independent audit has not been performed.
